# Bucket Words That Share the Same Letters

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/group-anagrams-2)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are given an array of strings `strs`. Partition the strings into groups so that two strings land in the same group exactly when one is an anagram of the other, meaning both contain the same characters with the same counts, just possibly arranged in a different order.

Return the collection of groups. The order of the groups in the result does not matter.

## Examples

**Example**

```text
Input: ["eat", "tea", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat"]
Output: [["ate","eat","tea"],["bat"],["nat","tan"]]
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Two strings are anagrams exactly when they share some canonical form, so look for a key that is identical for all members of a group.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a hash map from a canonical key (sorted letters or a character-count signature) to the list of words with that key.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Counting-based keys give roughly O(total characters) time versus sorting each word, and watch out for empty strings and duplicate words.

</details>
